dimensions.name: Lead / Round Dynamics
dimensions.evidence: Co-lead splits ID8's core signal: NEA re-ups, Kleiner Perkins is genuine new money; both are large, uncapacity-constrained funds, not forced sellers of access.

subcategories.name: Lead tier
subcategories.finding: NEA and Kleiner Perkins are both Tier 1 firms [[7]](https://www.kleinerperkins.com/people/josh-coyne/)

anchors.1: No credible institutional lead -- insider bridge, anonymous SPV, or a CVC/regional fund with no strategic relevance.
anchors.2: Non-Tier-1 VC leading the round.
anchors.3: Tier 1 VC (per the Tier 1 list) or a qualifying Domain-Strategic lead -- genuine category asymmetry, not a generic corporate CVC.
anchors.4: Tier 1+ VC (per the Tier 1+ list) leading the round.

subcategories.name: New vs re-up
subcategories.finding: NEA re-upped (led Series A [[1]](https://my.pitchbook.com/profile/606299-50/company/deals)); Kleiner Perkins is genuinely new money [[2]](https://my.pitchbook.com/profile/606299-50/company/profile)

anchors.1: Re-up claim taken at face value with no cap-table or prior-round corroboration -- unverifiable, treated as unconfirmed.
anchors.2: Confirmed re-up -- an existing investor increasing its position, not new money.
anchors.3: Re-up verified via cap table/prior-round disclosure, from a Tier 1+ firm, with strong stated conviction.
anchors.4: Verified new money -- the lead is on the cap table for the first time, ID8's strongest backtested predictor of returns.

subcategories.name: Stage fit
subcategories.finding: Series B primary, up round, $445M at $2.53B post-money [[1]](https://my.pitchbook.com/profile/606299-50/company/deals)

anchors.1: Pre-seed or Seed -- well outside mandate, no near-term path to Series B+.
anchors.2: Series A -- out of mandate for now but on a plausible path to Series B; file to Watch List.
anchors.3: Series B/C/D but the round has mixed characteristics (bridge-to-B, extension round) vs. a clean primary.
anchors.4: Clean primary round at Series B, C, or D -- squarely in mandate.

subcategories.name: Domain-strategic
subcategories.finding: Both leads are traditional financial VCs, no category asymmetry

anchors.1: Lead claims domain relevance but is a generic corporate CVC or regional fund with no genuine category asymmetry.
anchors.2: Lead is a traditional financial VC -- domain-strategic signal not applicable to this deal.
anchors.3: Lead has adjacent domain relevance but the asymmetry is partial (e.g. a fintech-adjacent bank, not a direct incumbent).
anchors.4: Lead is a large institutional player whose core business IS the company's market (NYSE/ICE-Polymarket precedent) -- genuine, direct asymmetry.

subcategories.name: Lead conviction
subcategories.finding: Named partners Coyne (KP) and Tretikov (NEA) have strong track records [[7]](https://www.kleinerperkins.com/people/josh-coyne/)[[8]](https://www.nea.com/news/press-releases/nea-appoints-lila-tretikov-partner-head-of-ai-strategy)

anchors.1: Deal sourced/led by a junior associate or scout check with no partner-level sponsorship visible.
anchors.2: A named partner is involved but with no visible personal track record or reputational stake disclosed.
anchors.3: The leading GP has a credible prior-fund track record and is the named partner driving the deal.
anchors.4: The leading GP is personally/reputationally committed -- strong prior-fund performance, personal co-invest, or a bio establishing direct conviction.

subcategories.name: Institutional momentum
subcategories.finding: NEA, Temasek, Prosus, Basis Set, Northzone all followed on from prior rounds [[1]](https://my.pitchbook.com/profile/606299-50/company/deals)

anchors.1: Existing investors from prior rounds are confirmed NOT participating -- a negative signal, insiders passing.
anchors.2: No visible signal either way on prior-round investor participation in this round.
anchors.3: Some prior-round investors are following on, but participation is partial or unconfirmed beyond a press mention.
anchors.4: Existing Tier-1 investors from prior rounds are confirmed following on alongside the new lead -- a distinct, corroborating signal.

subcategories.name: Existing Tier 1
subcategories.finding: Sequoia and Lightspeed (Tier 1+) held pre-round stakes since Seed [[1]](https://my.pitchbook.com/profile/606299-50/company/deals)

anchors.1: No Tier 1 or Tier 1+ investors anywhere on the pre-round cap table.
anchors.2: Cap table history is unclear/unverifiable, or only lower-tier/angel investors are confirmed.
anchors.3: At least one Tier 1 firm is confirmed on the pre-round cap table.
anchors.4: Multiple Tier 1/Tier 1+ firms are confirmed on the pre-round cap table -- a strong pre-existing pedigree signal.

subcategories.name: Timing/motivation
subcategories.finding: Valuation went ~$520M to $2.6B in under a year, oversubscribed [[4]](https://techfundingnews.com/cuspai-400m-series-b-2-6b-valuation-bezos-materials-search/)[[10]](https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/startups-tech/temasek-backed-cuspai-talks-boost-value-above-us1-billion-sources)

anchors.1: Defensive raise -- runway extension, down-round pressure, or limited alternatives visible.
anchors.2: Motivation is unclear or undisclosed; no evidence either of opportunistic strength or defensive need.
anchors.3: Opportunistic raise with at least one credible alternative term sheet or investor reported.
anchors.4: Clearly opportunistic -- positive inflection point, multiple credible term sheet options, company controlling the process.

dimensions.name: Founder / Team Quality
dimensions.evidence: Founders bring a genuine prior exit (Quantinuum) and elite AI pedigree, complemented by a materials-science CSO hire; recruiting and public credibility are exceptionally strong.

subcategories.name: Prior exit
subcategories.finding: Edwards co-founded CQC, merged into Quantinuum, now leading quantum computing firm [[5]](https://gbxglobal.org/cuspais-dr-chad-edwards-on-building-two-unicorns-before-turning-35/)

anchors.1: First-time founder(s) with no prior scaling or exit track record at all.
anchors.2: Some operating experience but nothing scaled meaningfully (no $100M+ ARR company, no exit).
anchors.3: First-time founder with elite pedigree (FAANG, top-tier academic, relevant domain leadership) but no exit yet.
anchors.4: Serial founder with a meaningful prior exit or a company scaled to $100M+ ARR.

subcategories.name: Domain authority
subcategories.finding: Edwards: chemistry PhD; Welling: AI4Science research, not materials-specific pre-founding [[6]](https://www.nea.com/blog/algorithms-to-atoms-our-investment-in-cuspai)

anchors.1: No prior experience in this market -- founders are entering a domain they've never operated in.
anchors.2: Adjacent but not direct domain experience (a related market, not this exact one).
anchors.3: Meaningful prior operating time in this exact market, though not in a senior/executive capacity.
anchors.4: Deep domain authority -- years as a practitioner, executive, or technical lead in this exact market before founding.

subcategories.name: Team complement
subcategories.finding: CEO (commercial), CTO (AI), CSO Walsh (materials science, Imperial) cover functions [[12]](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/news/articles/engineering/materials/2026/imperial-expert-leads-science-at-2-billion-ai-materials-company-cuspai/)

anchors.1: Solo founder or a founding team with duplicated skillsets and no coverage of a critical function.
anchors.2: Founding team has partial coverage but a visible, material gap (e.g. no technical co-founder for a deep-tech company).
anchors.3: Founding team covers the critical functions with reasonable but not ideal complementarity.
anchors.4: Clean technical/GTM/operational complementarity with no material coverage gap.

subcategories.name: Recruiting power (as in team growth)
subcategories.finding: Grew 3 to 100+ staff in 2 years; hired Hinton, LeCun [[9]](https://www.aicerts.ai/news/bezos-bets-400m-on-materials-discovery-ai-pioneer-cuspai/)

anchors.1: Headcount flat or shrinking; visible attrition among early/senior hires.
anchors.2: Headcount growth is slow or unverifiable from LinkedIn/public signal.
anchors.3: Steady headcount growth with some credible senior hires.
anchors.4: Strong LinkedIn headcount growth trend with notable senior hires and retention of early employees.

subcategories.name: Public presence
subcategories.finding: Press profiles (GBx, NEA, Imperial) plus academic/conference visibility for founders [[5]](https://gbxglobal.org/cuspais-dr-chad-edwards-on-building-two-unicorns-before-turning-35/)[[6]](https://www.nea.com/blog/algorithms-to-atoms-our-investment-in-cuspai)[[12]](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/news/articles/engineering/materials/2026/imperial-expert-leads-science-at-2-billion-ai-materials-company-cuspai/)

anchors.1: No public footprint at all for the founders -- cannot assess reputation.
anchors.2: Minimal public presence; thin press, no conference/technical presence found.
anchors.3: Regular press mentions or some conference/technical writing presence.
anchors.4: Strong, consistent public presence -- press, conference talks, technical writing, or open-source contributions hard to fabricate.

subcategories.name: Integrity
subcategories.finding: No red flags across CQC/Quantinuum, Imperial, NEA, press histories

anchors.1: Verified negative history -- litigation, fraud allegations, regulatory action, or confirmed toxic-culture signals.
anchors.2: Background is genuinely unverifiable after real search effort -- flag [unverified], a gap, not a red flag.
anchors.3: Background verified with no red flags found, though the search surface was limited.
anchors.4: Background thoroughly verified across multiple independent sources with no red flags found.

dimensions.name: AI Score
dimensions.evidence: Genuinely structural AI: proprietary architecture from a top ML researcher, reinforced by a named-partner data loop, though compounding improvement isn't yet quantified publicly.

subcategories.name: Ownership of models
subcategories.finding: Proprietary generative + physics-based models built by VAE co-inventor Welling [[6]](https://www.nea.com/blog/algorithms-to-atoms-our-investment-in-cuspai)

anchors.1: No proprietary model or fine-tune of any kind -- a thin wrapper calling a third-party foundation-model API with no differentiation.
anchors.2: Some fine-tuning or prompt/pipeline engineering on top of a third-party model, but no owned architecture.
anchors.3: A meaningfully customized or fine-tuned model with real engineering investment, though not a from-scratch architecture.
anchors.4: Proprietary architecture, training pipeline, or deeply fine-tuned model that is defensible and hard to replicate with a foundation-model update.

subcategories.name: Data flywheel / Recurssion
subcategories.finding: 45+ partner Foundry feeds lab-validation data back into models [[3]](https://www.vestbee.com/insights/articles/cusp-ai-raises-450-m)[[11]](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4615149-cuspai-nvidia-meta-join-bezos-backed-alliance-for-chipmaking-materials)

anchors.1: No evidence usage data feeds back into the product at all.
anchors.2: A plausible data flywheel is claimed but with no concrete evidence (no stated improvement cadence or proprietary dataset).
anchors.3: Some concrete evidence of a data flywheel (a proprietary dataset or a stated retraining cycle), though the compounding effect isn't yet demonstrated.
anchors.4: Strong, evidenced data flywheel -- usage data demonstrably compounds product quality over time via a proprietary dataset and an active retraining cycle.

dimensions.name: Terms
dimensions.evidence: No adverse public signal on carry, fees, or SPV structure for this round; standard ID8 terms assumed by default, not independently confirmed.

subcategories.name: Just assume they are good (unless there's something public)
subcategories.finding: No public ID8-specific terms found; assume standard 0/0/10 absent signal

anchors.1: Confirmed bad terms -- a recurring annual management fee (any amount), or carry >15% with an upfront fee >2%, or carry >20% regardless of fee.
anchors.2: Some public evidence of elevated but not disqualifying terms -- carry 10-15%, upfront access fee at or below 2% (the Polymarket standard), or limited information rights/multi-layer SPV.
anchors.3: Standard 0/0/10 terms confirmed, or no public evidence either way -- assume standard/good absent any adverse public signal.
anchors.4: Better than standard -- carry below 10% with pro-rata confirmed, full information rights, clean single-layer SPV or direct co-invest, no upfront fee.

dimensions.name: Fundamentals
dimensions.evidence: No confirmed revenue; a thin third-party ARR estimate implies a rich multiple, but named enterprise partnerships and TAM breadth are genuinely strong offsetting signals.

subcategories.name: Revenue/growth
subcategories.finding: [ESTIMATED] $3.8-7.5M ARR (3rd-party); below $25M bar despite 20x contract growth [[13]](https://newmarketpitch.com/blogs/news/generative-ai-cusp-ai-overvalued)[[14]](https://www.eweek.com/news/cuspai-ai-materials-funding/)

anchors.1: Confirmed sub-$5M ARR and sub-40% YoY growth -- a real, disclosed weak number, not a data gap.
anchors.2: No disclosed revenue/growth and no usable [ESTIMATED] triangulation exists, or an [ESTIMATED] figure lands below the $25M ARR / 70% growth bar.
anchors.3: $25M+ ARR with >70% YoY growth, confirmed or [ESTIMATED] via triangulation.
anchors.4: $50M+ ARR with 100%+ YoY growth, confirmed or [ESTIMATED] via triangulation.

subcategories.name: NDR
subcategories.finding: Not disclosed; no subscription NDR metric found or estimable

anchors.1: Confirmed NDR below 100% -- shrinking accounts.
anchors.2: NDR not disclosed and no usable estimate exists.
anchors.3: NDR above 110%, confirmed or credibly estimated from comparable-stage peers.
anchors.4: NDR above 130%, confirmed or credibly estimated from comparable-stage peers.

subcategories.name: Margins/unit econ
subcategories.finding: Gross margin/unit economics not disclosed; no usable estimate exists

anchors.1: Confirmed LTV/CAC below 2x -- growth is value-destroying.
anchors.2: Gross margin/unit economics not disclosed and no usable estimate exists.
anchors.3: LTV/CAC above 3x with reasonable gross margin -- growth is value-creating.
anchors.4: LTV/CAC above 5x with strong gross and contribution margin.

subcategories.name: Burn/runway
subcategories.finding: Burn not disclosed; 4Q2025 cash ($28.5M) looked low vs. capital raised

anchors.1: Confirmed burn above 100% of revenue -- burning faster than it earns with no offsetting signal.
anchors.2: Burn/runway not disclosed and no usable estimate exists.
anchors.3: Burn below 50% of revenue with a credible runway at current spend.
anchors.4: Burn below 20% of revenue -- strong capital discipline relative to revenue.

subcategories.name: Customer concentration
subcategories.finding: Multi-industry partners (Nvidia, Meta, Samsung, Hyundai, ASML, Kemira) suggest diversification [[3]](https://www.vestbee.com/insights/articles/cusp-ai-raises-450-m)[[11]](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4615149-cuspai-nvidia-meta-join-bezos-backed-alliance-for-chipmaking-materials)

anchors.1: Confirmed whale-contract risk -- a single customer or a small handful account for the clear majority of revenue.
anchors.2: Customer concentration not disclosed and cannot be estimated.
anchors.3: Some concentration in the top customers, but diversified enough that no single loss would be existential.
anchors.4: Broad, diversified customer base with no material single-customer or top-N concentration risk.

subcategories.name: Pref stack
subcategories.finding: Prior rounds show senior participating preferred; Series B terms undisclosed

anchors.1: Confirmed stacked, senior-heavy liquidation preference structure ahead of this round.
anchors.2: Cap table/pref stack structure not disclosed and cannot be estimated.
anchors.3: Preferred stack is reasonably lean, with no material senior-preference overhang identified.
anchors.4: Lean preferred stack confirmed -- clean capital structure that protects downside and signals capital discipline.

subcategories.name: Moat durability
subcategories.finding: 45+ enterprise Foundry partners plus Hinton/LeCun advisors form real moat [[3]](https://www.vestbee.com/insights/articles/cusp-ai-raises-450-m)[[11]](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4615149-cuspai-nvidia-meta-join-bezos-backed-alliance-for-chipmaking-materials)

anchors.1: Moat is purely narrative ("great team," "we move fast") with no structural defensibility identified.
anchors.2: Some structural elements claimed but not clearly evidenced (e.g. asserted network effects with no usage data).
anchors.3: Real but moderate structural moat -- some combination of switching costs, early network effects, or a regulatory edge.
anchors.4: Strong structural moat -- durable network effects, a genuine regulatory barrier, or high switching costs, clearly evidenced.

subcategories.name: Market/TAM
subcategories.finding: Materials R&D spans semis, batteries, carbon capture, clean energy -- venture-scale

anchors.1: Current market is not venture-scale and no credible adjacent expansion path exists.
anchors.2: Market size or expansion path is unclear/undisclosed and cannot be credibly estimated.
anchors.3: Current market alone is venture-scale, though the adjacent expansion path is more aspirational than in-motion.
anchors.4: Current market is venture-scale and a credible, already-in-motion adjacent expansion path is evidenced.

subcategories.name: Valuation vs comps
subcategories.finding: Implied 347-684x revenue vs. XtalPi's public 26.8x multiple -- rich [[13]](https://newmarketpitch.com/blogs/news/generative-ai-cusp-ai-overvalued)[[16]](https://multiples.vc/public-comps/xtalpi-valuation-multiples)

anchors.1: Entry valuation is confirmed materially rich vs. growth-adjusted public/private comps.
anchors.2: No public revenue multiple available and no usable [ESTIMATED]/comp-set triangulation exists -- write [NOT PUBLIC].
anchors.3: Entry multiple is defensible vs. public/private comps on a growth-adjusted (Rule-of-40-style) basis, confirmed or [ESTIMATED].
anchors.4: Entry multiple is favorable vs. growth-adjusted comps -- priced at a discount to what the growth/margin profile would justify.

subcategories.name: Sector risk
subcategories.finding: DeepMind/Microsoft open materials-gen models compete; physical-synthesis partnerships differentiate [[15]](https://www.technologyreview.com/2025/12/15/1129210/ai-materials-science-discovery-startups-investment/)[[17]](https://pitchbook.com/news/articles/discovering-new-materials-with-ai-has-a-winding-road-to-vc-returns)

anchors.1: Confirmed acute disruption risk -- foundational-model capability creep, pending regulatory action, or macro cyclicality that could impair the business within the hold period.
anchors.2: Sector risk is unclear or unassessed from available evidence.
anchors.3: Some sector exposure identified but manageable -- not an acute, near-term threat.
anchors.4: Sector is not at acute disruption risk -- durable position against foundational-model creep, regulatory shifts, and macro cyclicality.

dimensions.name: Return Potential
dimensions.evidence: Base-case 6x is a stretch at this entry: sector's only public comp trades far smaller; some exit optionality exists via strategics and an IPO precedent.

subcategories.name: Entry multiple
subcategories.finding: Rich vs. estimated revenue and nascent-sector comps; hard to justify confidently [[13]](https://newmarketpitch.com/blogs/news/generative-ai-cusp-ai-overvalued)[[16]](https://multiples.vc/public-comps/xtalpi-valuation-multiples)

anchors.1: Entry multiple is not justified even after accounting for growth and margin trajectory.
anchors.2: Entry multiple cannot be assessed -- insufficient data on growth/margin trajectory to judge.
anchors.3: Entry multiple is justified once growth and margin trajectory are factored in, though not favorable.
anchors.4: Entry multiple is well justified -- growth-adjusted pricing is attractive relative to trajectory.

subcategories.name: Base-case MOIC
subcategories.finding: 6x needs ~$15B+ exit; largest public comp (XtalPi) is $4B [[16]](https://multiples.vc/public-comps/xtalpi-valuation-multiples)

anchors.1: Below 2x MOIC / below 10% IRR as the realistic base case.
anchors.2: 2-3x MOIC / 10-20% IRR -- below venture scale in the base case.
anchors.3: 3-6x MOIC / 20-30% IRR as a realistic base case, with some execution risk.
anchors.4: 6x+ MOIC / 30%+ IRR as the base case (not the bull case), with a credible path shown.

subcategories.name: Exit path
subcategories.finding: XtalPi's public listing is a sector precedent; strategic acquirers among partners [[16]](https://multiples.vc/public-comps/xtalpi-valuation-multiples)

anchors.1: No credible exit path identified -- no IPO readiness signal, no M&A appetite, no comparable precedent exits.
anchors.2: Exit path is unclear or speculative, with only weak precedent.
anchors.3: A reasonable exit path exists (IPO readiness or active M&A appetite in the sector) with some precedent support.
anchors.4: Clear exit path -- strong IPO readiness or active M&A appetite in the sector, with genuinely comparable precedent exits.

subcategories.name: Dilution
subcategories.finding: No future-round dilution modeling available at this stage of screen

anchors.1: Dilution modeling was not attempted, or the deal isn't viable even under a favorable dilution assumption.
anchors.2: Dilution is modeled loosely or with unsupported assumptions.
anchors.3: At least two future financing rounds (~20-25% each) are explicitly modeled before exit, with a viable resulting MOIC.
anchors.4: Dilution is rigorously modeled across multiple future rounds and the return case holds up well even under conservative assumptions.

subcategories.name: Time to liquidity
subcategories.finding: Series B, early; liquidity likely 5+ years out, unmodeled precisely

anchors.1: Time to liquidity is long with no offsetting IRR -- the modeled MOIC only works over an unrealistically extended hold.
anchors.2: Time to liquidity is unclear or unmodeled.
anchors.3: A reasonable time-to-liquidity estimate exists and the resulting IRR is acceptable, even if not exceptional.
anchors.4: Time to liquidity is modeled explicitly and the resulting IRR is strong -- the same MOIC compressed into a shorter, credible hold.

subcategories.name: Downside protection
subcategories.finding: No disclosed downside terms for a hypothetical ID8 co-invest structure

anchors.1: No meaningful downside protection -- weak or absent liquidation preference, pro-rata, or seniority; for secondaries, a premium paid vs. last priced round.
anchors.2: Downside protection terms are undisclosed or unclear.
anchors.3: Standard downside protection in place -- reasonable liquidation preference, pro-rata rights, and seniority.
anchors.4: Strong downside protection -- favorable liquidation preference/seniority, or for secondaries, a confirmed discount vs. last priced round.

subcategories.name: Exit multiples
subcategories.finding: XtalPi is the closest comp but differs (pharma/robotics hybrid, China) [[16]](https://multiples.vc/public-comps/xtalpi-valuation-multiples)

anchors.1: Exit-multiple assumptions rely on aspirational comps from a different category or a cycle peak, not a genuinely comparable precedent set.
anchors.2: No genuinely comparable exit precedent set could be identified.
anchors.3: Exit-multiple assumptions are anchored to a reasonably comparable precedent set.
anchors.4: Exit-multiple assumptions are anchored to a genuinely comparable, well-evidenced precedent set.

subcategories.name: Secondary demand
subcategories.finding: No Setter 30 or Forge/Caplight listing found; too new to trade

anchors.1: No secondary market signal found, or the company is reported as actively avoided/discounted in secondary trading.
anchors.2: Secondary market activity/demand could not be assessed from available sources.
anchors.3: Some secondary market interest signal exists but not on a named tracked list (Setter 30) or major marketplace.
anchors.4: Company appears on the Setter Capital "Setter 30" or is reported as actively traded by Forge/Caplight/EquityZen or similar -- external corroboration of the exit thesis.

screen.rationale: CuspAI mostly aligns with ID8's thesis: genuine new-money Tier 1 (Kleiner Perkins) co-leads alongside a verified NEA re-up, and AI is structurally the moat, not a feature. But undisclosed revenue and a fast, rich re-rating temper conviction on return potential.
